1.why: All seven screens are static single-column cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up dialogs anywhere.

2.why: Headings are coloured, the one primary action is a solid blue button, and each card holds a single field, though the large dark Logs block competes for attention.

3.why: Each step shows only one task, but the goal-relevant item (e.g. the token) must be hunted out of the Logs panel and the first field asks for a vague 'non-identifying contact value'.

4.why: She must carry a 40-character token and a six-digit code from the Logs panel into input fields plus recall a 4-part password rule, so several things must be held in mind.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing is saved or pre-filled for recognition; the only identifiers shown are a random opaque token and a numeric code.

7.why: Sentences are short, but wording such as 'non-identifying contact value', 'mock delivery', 'MFA', and 'single-use tokens tied to this secure browser session' is technical.

8.why: No error or validation message is visible in any of the seven screenshots, so problem-plus-fix messaging is not demonstrated.

9.why: Only abstract rules are given ('Use 12 or more characters…', 'six-digit code'); no sample input or worked example is shown.

10.why: The single password + emailed-code path is described plainly, but no alternative sign-in choices (biometric, passkey) are offered or labelled.

11.why: Every screen presents one field and one button, never competing options.

12.why: Each action produces an explicit outcome ('Sign-in confirmed', 'Privacy conditions accepted') plus timestamped log lines confirming what happened.

13.why: Each card has a one-line instruction and a standing security tip, but there is no help link, tooltip, or guidance on where to find the token.

14.why: No back, resend-code, restart, or edit control is visible on any step, so recovering from a mis-entry is not supported on screen.

15.why: Header, card layout, typography, button style, security notice, and Logs panel are identical across all seven steps.
